label: def:quantum-bloch-group
title: Quantum Bloch group and the pentagon identity
html:
The classical Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) is defined by the five-term relation of the dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2. The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q)(R) replaces this with the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q:

  \Phi_q(u)\,\Phi_q(v)
  \;=\;
  \Phi_q(v)\,\Phi_q(uv)\,\Phi_q(u)
  \qquad \text{where } uv = qvu

In the form e_q(a)\,e_q(b) = e_q(b)\,e_q(-ba)\,e_q(a) with ab = qba, this is the Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon relation, a quantum analogue of the Rogers five-term relation [kirillov1995, §2.5, Thm. I and Cor. 11]. This identity is the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form.

The connection to the QOU framework — why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm, the Kashaev invariant, and the pre-archimedean refinement of \mathfrak{B}(q) over the Habiro ring — is developed in the follow-on remark. A functorial setting for state-sum invariants built from quantum dilogarithms is quantum hyperbolic field theory: for each odd N it assigns to a 3-manifold with a framed tangle and a PSL(2,\mathbb{C})-character a tensor built from matrix dilogarithms [baseilhac-benedetti2007, §1, §2.1].

Branch ambiguity and the extended Bloch group (literature). The ordinary Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) carries the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function, which recovers only the volume. The multivaluedness of \mathrm{Li}_2 is removed by passing to the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of Goette and Zickert, as surveyed in [arxiv-2304.12545v1, §3]: generators are pairs [u,v] with e^u + e^v = 1, the relations are a lifted version of the five-term relation, and the regulator \sum_j [u_j,v_j] \mapsto \sum_j \bigl(L(v_j) + \tfrac12 u_j v_j - \tfrac{\pi^2}{6}\bigr), with L(v) = \mathrm{Li}_2(1-e^v), is well defined modulo 4\pi^2 on that relation. It is the extended group, not the ordinary one, on which a complex-valued dilogarithm invariant is single-valued. The survey is a secondary source: the lifted five-term relation is stated there without proof, and the primary papers of Goette and Zickert are not in the bibliography. Neumann's original construction is registered [neumann2004, §1]. The volume computations in this chapter use only the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function D on the ordinary Bloch group rather than the lifted five-term relation on \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}).
